zh: 按原始下标的奇偶给元素染色，跟踪删除过程：删除一个内部系统时，它左右两个邻居颜色相同，合并后仍是同一颜色原值之和。
因此最后剩下的系统一定是某一种奇偶类的非空子集之和。有正数时上界是该类全部正数之和，并且可以先删两端、再删该类内部的非正值、最后删间隔元素来达到；没有正数时只能留下一个最大元素。
一次扫描：分别累加偶数下标和奇数下标上的正值，同时记录全局最大值；两个和中较大者为正就输出它，否则输出全局最大元素（可能为 0 或负数）。结果可达 10^14，用 64 位整数。
en: Color the elements by the parity of their original index and follow the deletions: when an interior system is deleted, its left and right neighbors have the same color, so the merged system is still a sum of original values of one color.

Hence the final system is always the sum of a non-empty subset of one parity class. With positive values, the bound is the sum of all positive values in that class, and it is reached by trimming both ends, deleting the class's interior non-positive systems, then deleting the separating systems; with no positive value, only one largest element can be kept.

In one pass, add up the positive values at even indices and at odd indices separately while tracking the global maximum; if the larger sum is positive output it, otherwise output the global maximum element (which may be 0 or negative). The result can reach 10^14, so use 64-bit integers.

explanationEn:
## Source correction

fastprep/Amazon/amazon-get-max-charge.md at the fixed commit e66f809f4c953bce129f68491726176615db6afc states explicitly: delete the chosen system; if it has both a left and a right neighbor, the two neighbors automatically merge, and the merged charge is the sum of the two neighbors; the deleted element's own value is not counted. An endpoint is simply deleted. On this basis this site corrects the inconsistent descriptions in the early catalog, such as "add its own value to the neighbors", "delete any interior element" and "maximum contiguous subarray".

The three examples of the main raw text have outputs 4, 9 and 3; for the first example [-2,4,3,-2,1] the catalog mistakenly wrote 9, and this site publicly corrects it to 4. The main raw text only says the maximum obtainable charge, while amazon-maximum-charge-after-removal.md in the same commit states explicitly that the process continues until only one system remains; the two optimal values are equivalent, because any intermediate system can eventually be kept alone by repeatedly deleting the other systems at both ends. This site does not reuse the incorrect operation interpretations of other raw variants and does not execute the source's solution code.

The source ranges 1≤n≤200000 and −10^9≤charge[i]≤10^9 are kept in full; the standard input/output protocol is this site's addition. Exactly one system must remain at the end, so the answer for an all-negative array must not be written as the 0 of an empty set.

## Algorithm

Separately add up all positive values at the 0-based even indices and at the odd indices of the original array. If a positive number exists, the answer is the larger of the two sums; otherwise the answer is the largest element of the original array (which may be 0 or negative).

## Correctness

Color the original indices with two colors by parity. Two invariants always hold: every current system is the sum of a group of original values of the same color, and the colors of the current systems alternate. Both clearly hold initially; deleting an endpoint keeps the alternation; when an interior system is deleted, its left and right neighbors have the same color, and after they merge both invariants still hold. Therefore the final system can only consist of a non-empty subset of one parity class of the original array. When positive numbers exist, its sum does not exceed the sum of all positive numbers in that class; when there are none, the sum of any non-empty subset does not exceed the global maximum element.

To reach the positive upper bound, choose the parity class with the larger positive sum. First keep deleting endpoints to remove the elements before that class's first positive value and after its last positive value. Then delete, one by one, the interior non-positive systems of that class; these deletions only merge neighbors of the other class and do not harm the target positive values. Now consecutive target positive values are separated by exactly one system of the other class; deleting these separating systems in turn merges all target positive values into their sum. If there is no positive value, keep one largest element by deleting from both ends. Every upper bound is attainable, so the algorithm is correct.

## Complexity and integer range

O(n) time and O(1) extra computation space; the reference program's input tokenization still needs O(n) space. The largest result is 100000×10^9=10^14, so Java/C++/Go should use 64-bit integers. When n=1 no operation is needed.

## Valid example walkthroughs and independent verification

In the first example, delete the left end −2 to get [4,3,−2,1], then delete the right ends 1, −2 and 3 in a row, leaving 4. In the second example keep deleting at both ends until 9 remains; in the third example delete the left end −1 and the right end 2, leaving 3. A supplementary example showing a real merge: deleting the middle −100 of [4,−100,5] merges the two neighbors into 9, which also shows this is not a Kadane problem.

The independent oracle enumerates every deletable position state by state: an endpoint is simply removed; an interior deletion removes the system itself and replaces these three systems with the sum of its left and right neighbors, recursing until the length is 1 and taking the maximum result over all operation sequences. It does not use the parity formula. 163 distinct small inputs were compared one by one with the reference program through real Python subprocesses; full-scale cases compute their expected values with directly provable same-sign or alternating structures. Both faulty programs exit normally and are rejected by the official cases.
